clauses.reason: The opening paragraphs of the order ("I hereby declare a national emergency to deal with that threat. I hereby order") declare a national emergency to deal with the threat that attachment and other judicial process poses to the Development Fund for Iraq and Iraqi petroleum. The declaration has no end date of its own. It was expanded in scope by EO 13315 (effective 2003-08-29), kept as the basis of other authorities by EO 13350 (effective 2004-07-30), modified in scope by EO 13364 (2004-11-29) and, when EO 13668 terminated the sec. 1 prohibitions on 2014-05-27, expressly left in place: that order says the action "is not intended otherwise to affect the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13303 of May 22, 2003, as expanded in scope by Executive Order 13315 of August 28, 2003, which shall remain in place". Under the National Emergencies Act the emergency lapses on its anniversary unless the President continues it by notice. The held Federal Register notices show a continuation signed each year from 2004 to 2026, and the last, the Notice of May 4, 2026, says the emergency "must continue in effect beyond May 22, 2026" and continues it "for 1 year", so on 2026-10-14 the emergency was in effect. Each notice is a later event on this clause with its signing date.

This clause ("Section 1. Unless licensed or otherwise authorized pursuant to this order, any attachment, judgment, decree, lien, execution, garnishment, or other judicial process is") is part of the sec. 1 prohibition on attachment, judgment, lien, execution and other judicial process against the Development Fund for Iraq and Iraqi petroleum and its proceeds. EO 13364 (signed 2004-11-29, no separate effective date) restated sec. 1 with a new subsection (a) listing the Fund, the petroleum "only until title passes to the initial purchaser" and Central Bank of Iraq property, and a new subsection (b) excepting final judgments on contracts entered into by the Government of Iraq after 2004-06-30, so the clause continued, amended, from 2004-11-29 (the restatement is a later event; the reviewer should note it changed the substance). EO 13668 then ended it: "The prohibitions set forth in section 1 of Executive Order 13303 of May 22, 2003, as amended by Executive Order 13364 of November 29, 2004, are hereby terminated." The order has no separate effective-date clause, so the termination took effect on signing, 2014-05-27 (published 2014-05-29). That termination reaches the whole of sec. 1 as amended, including sec. 1.

clauses.reason: Sec. 2 ("Sec. 2. (a) As of the effective date of this order, Executive Order 12722 of August 2, 1990, Executive Order 12724 of August 9, 1990, and Executive Order 13290 of March 20, 2003, shall not apply to the property and") says that, as of the effective date of the order, EOs 12722, 12724 and 13290 shall not apply to the property described in sec. 1, and that nothing in the order affects rules, licenses and other administrative action issued under those orders or under IEEPA and the UNPA, except as terminated, modified or suspended by the issuing agency. EO 13350 (effective 2004-07-30) revoked EO 12722 and EO 12724 and amended EO 13290 so that it rests on the national emergency declared in EO 13303, so after that date the clause has no object as to the two revoked orders and continues only as to EO 13290; EO 13668 terminated the sec. 1 prohibitions but did not mention sec. 2. No held source ends sec. 2 as to EO 13290, and an exemption that is overtaken is not an ended command, so the clause is recorded as operative and the reviewer should note that its practical reach has narrowed.

clauses.reason: Sec. 2(b) ("(b) Nothing in this order is intended to affect the continued effectiveness of any rules, regulations, orders, licenses or other forms of administrative action issued, taken, or continued in effect") preserves rules, regulations, orders and licenses issued under EOs 12722, 12724 or 13290 or under IEEPA and the UNPA, except as the issuing agency terminates, modifies or suspends them. It is a standing preservation of administrative action; it ends only through the issuing agencies' own acts or a revocation of the order, and none is in the held evidence. EO 13350 revoked EOs 12722 and 12724 (effective 2004-07-30) but its sec. 1 determined under IEEPA section 207(a) that continuing the prohibitions on property blocked under those orders was necessary on account of claims involving Iraq, so the preserved actions are not shown to have ended with the revocation.

research_rationale:
The held official Federal Register text of EO 13303 (68 FR 31931, FR Doc. 03-13412, published 2003-05-28) was read in full. It declares a national emergency over the threat of judicial process against the Development Fund for Iraq and Iraqi petroleum, prohibits attachment and similar process against them (sec. 1), carves the property out of EOs 12722, 12724 and 13290 (sec. 2), defines terms (sec. 3), authorises the Treasury to implement (sec. 4) and has the usual disclaimers. The 16-clause inventory covers the opening paragraphs, each section and each lettered definition and was confirmed against the text. Sec. 1 and its subsections ended on 2014-05-27 when EO 13668 terminated the sec. 1 prohibitions as amended by EO 13364, a termination that by its own words left the national emergency in place. The emergency is continued each May by a notice: all 23 notices from 2004 to 2026 are held and attached as later events to the lead clause, the last signed 2026-05-04, which carries the emergency past 2026-05-22 and so through 2026-10-14. The Office of the Federal Register catalogue lists the order as amended by EO 13364 with no revocation. The U.S. Code search covers editions current through 2026-10-09, so a law enacted from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 is not reflected. The authority statutes (IEEPA, the National Emergencies Act, the United Nations Participation Act) are cited in the order and referred to in the 2026 notice as the basis of the continued emergency; no held source shows any of them repealed or expired.

savings.reason: EO 13303 has no savings clause of its own. Its sec. 2(b) preserves administrative action taken under EOs 12722, 12724 and 13290 or under IEEPA and the UNPA. EO 13350 later revoked EO 12722 and EO 12724 and, in its sec. 1, continued the prohibitions on property blocked under them, and EO 13668 terminated the sec. 1 prohibitions with a statement that the national emergency remains in place, so the continuing effects of the order are carried by the emergency, by its continuation notices and by the implementing authority, which is why the savings state is transferred or accrued.
